title: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
summary: Given an n x n grid where each cell is either empty (0) or contains a thief (1), find the path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) with the highest safeness factor.
statement: Given an n x n grid where each cell is either empty (0) or contains a thief (1), find the path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) with the highest safeness factor. The safeness factor of a path is the minimum Manhattan distance from any cell on the path to the nearest thief. Adjacent cells are those directly north, south, east, or west. The Manhattan distance between two cells (a,b) and (x,y) is |a-x| + |b-y|.
constraints: grid is n by n with at least one thief; movement is four-directional and may enter thief cells.
A path score is its minimum distance to any thief; maximize that score from top-left to bottom-right.
hints: First compute each cell’s nearest-thief distance with multi-source BFS.
Then run a widest-path search whose path value is the minimum cell distance seen.
Pop the currently safest frontier and push neighbors with min(path, neighbor distance).
The max-heap settles each cell at the largest possible bottleneck, exactly the safeness definition.
editorial: The max-heap settles each cell at the largest possible bottleneck, exactly the safeness definition.

tests.explanation: Both endpoints contain thieves, so every path has safeness zero.
A route along the left and bottom edges stays at least distance two from the thief.
